issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify that Farm.animals is a List<Animal> and that an ArrayList should be used/initialized in the no-arg constructor, but the solution implementation uses a Set<Animal> (HashSet) for the animals attribute and its getter/setter. This is a structural mismatch that could confuse students about the intended collection type and behavior (ordering, duplicates) and prevents direct reliance on the solution as a canonical example of the requested List/ArrayList design.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem statement by changing Farm.animals to type List<Animal> and initializing it as an ArrayList in the no-arg constructor (and update getter/setter signatures accordingly). Alternatively, update the problem statement/UML to accept Set semantics if using a Set was intentional.

issues.description: The template's singFarmSongVerse method signature has the Animal parameter commented out (private void singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/)), whereas the UML and solution expect singFarmSongVerse to accept an Animal parameter. This mismatch between the template stub and the specified method signature can confuse students about the correct method signature to implement or call.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template method signature to match the UML and solution (private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)) so students have a correct stub to implement and call. If the commented parameter was intentional, add a clarifying comment in the template explaining that students should modify the signature to accept an Animal.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML explicitly require the Farm to use a List (ArrayList) to hold its animals, but the solution implementation declares the collection as a Set (HashSet). Although the attribute name 'animals' is consistent, the collection type identifier differs (List/ArrayList vs Set/HashSet). This creates a conceptual mismatch for students who are instructed to initialize an ArrayList in the no-arg constructor and expect list semantics (ordering, possible duplicates).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem statement by using the same collection type: change the Farm implementation to use List<Animal> and initialize it with new ArrayList<>(); update imports and getter/setter signatures accordingly. Alternatively, update the problem statement/UML to accept Set/HashSet if unordered, unique collection semantics are intended.
